turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you for seeing me. Um, well, to be completely honest, what really pushed me to finally pick up the phone and make this appointment is... well, it's this ongoing issue at work that's just getting to be too much. I'm an auditor, and I also do a lot of these mentorship events for the junior accountants at my firm, which is a lot to juggle, I know, but I've usually managed. 

But lately, I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits or after a big mentorship seminar, and I sit down at my desk with every single intention of finishing them right then and there. I mean, I'll even pull up all the files, review the spreadsheets, and start typing. But then... I don't even know how it happens, but days will go by, and I'll find out—usually because a partner or a mentee asks me about it—that the final email never actually went out, or the review note never got uploaded to the system, or the feedback form just never got done. It's just sitting there in my drafts or half-filled out on my desk. And it's incredibly frustrating because I genuinely thought I had finished it, and at 47, with my level of experience in accounting, I just shouldn't be dropping the ball on the very last step like this over and over again. It makes me look careless, and I'm really not, I just... I don't know where the disconnect is between starting the task and actually clicking send, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly describes failing to finish workplace duties, such as leaving emails in drafts or forms half-filled out, despite intending to complete them.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you struggle with finishing tasks or staying organized in a similar way?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, wow, yes. Um, it's funny you ask that because... well, it’s not really funny, it’s actually kind of a sore subject sometimes when my family gets together. But yes, absolutely. If you were to go back and look at my old report cards, like, even way back in elementary school—I grew up in this small district where the teachers wrote these really long, handwritten comments on the back of the card, you know? And every single one of them, I mean practically every year, it was the exact same story. 

They would always start by saying how bright I was, which was nice, I guess, but then it would just be this laundry list of things I was doing wrong. They’d say I was always losing my assignments, or that I rushed past all the small details on my worksheets just to get them done, which, as an auditor now, is just incredibly ironic. And they always mentioned that I talked out of turn. I was constantly getting in trouble for blurting things out or chatting with my neighbor when I was supposed to be working. And the teachers were always having to come over to my desk and tap on it to remind me to actually finish my work. It was like I’d do the first half of a math sheet and then my brain would just be somewhere else entirely, completely forgetting there was a back page. 

My mother... oh my goodness, my mother still jokes about it to this day, which, honestly, gets a little old. She loves to tell people at dinner parties how I could completely ace a spelling test or a history quiz without even trying, but then I would completely forget to turn in the big project that was literally sitting right there in my backpack. I'd carry it back and forth to school for a week, squishing it, and never take it out to hand it to the teacher. So, yeah, it’s definitely not a new thing, this whole... not finishing the last step business. It’s just that back then it was a school project and now it’s an audit report, you know? It's just so frustrating that I'm still doing the exact same thing forty years later.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient states they 'rushed past all the small details' on their worksheets.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient describes needing reminders to 'actually finish my work' and failing to turn in completed projects.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly mentions 'losing my assignments' during school.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient notes their 'brain would just be somewhere else entirely' while trying to work.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient reports they were constantly getting in trouble for 'talked out of turn' and 'blurting things out'.
